codeReview.summary: Well-implemented per-domain proxy assignment feature with solid test coverage. The implementation correctly adds dropdowns for Gmail, Yahoo, and Hotmail domains, integrates with backend Tauri commands, and properly handles the per-domain rotation mode. All expected behaviors from the feature description are met.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker defined an inline interface `ProxyPool` inside the error handler (settings-content.tsx:174-176) rather than importing from a shared types file. While this works, it creates a maintenance burden if the backend structure changes.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/components/settings/settings-content.tsx:174-176 — inline `interface ProxyPool { domain_assignments: Record<string, string>; }` instead of importing from use-settings.ts where BackendProxyPool already exists

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker followed the fullstack-worker skill procedure correctly - wrote tests first (red), implemented backend (though backend was already in place from prior commits), then frontend, then ran integration tests. Skill procedure matches reality.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Transcript shows TDD approach with 15 per-domain tests and 4 integration tests. skillFeedback.followedProcedure is true with no deviations.

summary: PASS. The per-domain proxy assignment feature is well-implemented with comprehensive test coverage (19 new tests). The UI correctly shows dropdowns for Gmail, Yahoo, and Hotmail only when Per-Domain rotation mode is selected. Assignments are persisted to the backend via Tauri commands (assign_domain_proxy, unassign_domain_proxy). Backend validation logic correctly uses domain assignments through get_proxy_for_email method. All expected behaviors from validation contract VAL-CFG-013 and VAL-CFG-014 are satisfied. No blocking issues found.
